name: use-godig-not-memory
description: Tests that for a Go package API question the model uses the godig pkg.go.dev client rather than answering from (potentially stale) training memory
prompt: What does the github.com/samber/lo Map function's signature look like in the latest version, and how do I use it? I need the exact current signature, not a guess.
trap: A skill-less model answers the signature from memory, which may be outdated or wrong, instead of verifying it against pkg.go.dev

assertions.text: Uses godig to look up the symbol rather than answering purely from memory
Uses the godig 'symbol doc' command (e.g. godig symbol doc github.com/samber/lo Map) rather than fetching the whole package doc
Passes the full import path github.com/samber/lo as the positional argument
Passes -o md so the result renders as Markdown in chat
Does not invent or assert a signature without sourcing it from pkg.go.dev/godig

name: start-with-overview
description: Tests that the model starts with the compact 'overview' command for a general package summary instead of pulling large per-facet output
prompt: Give me a quick rundown of the github.com/samber/ro module — what is the latest version, what license is it under, and does it have any obvious problems? Keep it compact.
trap: A skill-less model issues several separate heavyweight calls (module info + versions + licenses + vulns) or fetches large doc/readme output when one compact overview call suffices

assertions.text: Uses the godig 'overview' command as the starting point (e.g. godig overview github.com/samber/ro)
Notes that overview returns a compact summary including metadata, latest/recent versions, license types, and vulnerabilities in a single call
Does NOT pull a LARGE command (package doc, module readme, or licenses full text) for this compact summary
Uses -o md for the output
Passes the full import path github.com/samber/ro as the positional argument

name: check-vulnerabilities
description: Tests that the model uses godig vulns to check for known CVEs/vulnerabilities rather than guessing or relying on memory
prompt: Before I add github.com/dgrijalva/jwt-go to my Go project, I want to know whether it has any known security vulnerabilities. How do I check?
trap: A skill-less model claims a package is safe/unsafe from memory, or directs the user to manually browse a website, instead of querying the vuln database via godig

assertions.text: Uses the godig 'vulns' command (e.g. godig vulns github.com/dgrijalva/jwt-go) to check for known vulnerabilities
Notes that the data comes from pkg.go.dev (the Go vulnerability database), not from the model's memory
Notes that vulns returns an empty list when a module has no known vulnerabilities
Uses -o md for the output
Does not assert a definitive vulnerability verdict without sourcing it from godig/pkg.go.dev

name: list-available-versions
description: Tests that the model uses godig versions (newest-first) to enumerate available module versions instead of guessing
prompt: What versions of github.com/samber/lo are available, and which is the newest? I want to see the actual published versions.
trap: A skill-less model lists version numbers from memory or suggests running `go list -m -versions`, instead of querying pkg.go.dev via godig versions

assertions.text: Uses the godig 'versions' command (e.g. godig versions github.com/samber/lo) to list available versions
Notes that versions are returned newest-first
Mentions that the listing auto-paginates (returns all results) and that --limit can cap the output
Uses -o md for the output
Does not enumerate specific version numbers purely from memory

name: filter-syntax-symbols
description: Tests correct use of the --filter Go boolean expression to narrow list results server-side, including correct field names and capitalized kind values
prompt: From github.com/samber/lo, I only want the exported functions whose names start with "Map". How do I list just those with godig?
trap: A skill-less model passes a regex, uses a lowercase kind value like 'func', or filters client-side; it does not know --filter takes a Go boolean expression with capitalized kind values and string functions like hasPrefix

assertions.text: Uses the godig 'symbols' command with a --filter expression (e.g. godig symbols github.com/samber/lo --filter '...')
Filters on kind using the capitalized value "Function" (e.g. kind=="Function"), not a lowercase value like 'func'
Uses the hasPrefix(name, "Map") string function for the name-prefix condition rather than a regex
Combines the two conditions with the && operator
Wraps the whole filter expression in single quotes for the shell
Treats --filter as a Go boolean expression evaluated server-side, not as a regex

name: who-imports-package
description: Tests that the model uses godig imported-by to find packages that import a target, rather than suggesting a code/GitHub search
prompt: I want to see which Go packages import github.com/samber/ro, so I can gauge how it's used in the wild. How do I find that?
trap: A skill-less model suggests GitHub code search, grep.app, or sourcegraph, unaware that pkg.go.dev exposes importers directly via godig imported-by

assertions.text: Uses the godig 'imported-by' command (e.g. godig imported-by github.com/samber/ro) to list importing packages
Notes that --limit can cap the number of results returned
Uses -o md for the output
Does not primarily recommend an external tool (GitHub search, Sourcegraph, grep.app) instead of godig for this

name: prefer-godig-over-context7
description: Tests that for Go package docs the model prefers godig/pkg.go.dev over Context7 or generic web docs
prompt: I need the documentation for the Go package github.com/samber/lo to understand its API. I usually use Context7 for library docs — should I use that here?
trap: A skill-less model defaults to Context7 or a generic doc fetch for the Go package, instead of preferring the pkg.go.dev-backed godig client

assertions.text: Recommends using godig (pkg.go.dev) for the Go package documentation
States a preference for godig over Context7 for Go packages/modules specifically
Shows a concrete godig command to get the docs (e.g. godig package doc or godig symbol doc for github.com/samber/lo)
Uses -o md (or notes -o md renders the docs as Markdown in chat)

name: symbol-doc-over-package-doc
description: Tests that the model scopes documentation to a single symbol when only one symbol is needed, rather than pulling the entire (LARGE) package doc
prompt: I only need to understand the OopsError.Error method from github.com/samber/oops — just that one method's signature and runnable example. How do I look it up efficiently?
trap: A skill-less model fetches the entire package doc/examples (LARGE, token-heavy) when a single-symbol lookup would suffice

assertions.text: Uses 'symbol doc' for the one symbol's signature/doc (e.g. godig symbol doc github.com/samber/oops OopsError.Error)
Uses 'symbol examples' for that symbol's runnable example (e.g. godig symbol examples github.com/samber/oops OopsError.Error)
Explicitly avoids the package-wide 'package doc'/'package examples' commands, noting they are LARGE/token-heavy
Notes that the single-symbol commands are more token-efficient than the package-wide ones
Uses -o md for the output

name: parallelize-independent-lookups
description: Tests that the model parallelizes independent read-only godig lookups instead of running them sequentially, and dispatches sub-agents for large fan-outs
prompt: I'm evaluating three Go libraries — github.com/samber/lo, github.com/samber/mo, and github.com/samber/do. For each, I want the overview, the latest version, and any known vulnerabilities. What's the most efficient way to gather all this with godig?
trap: A skill-less model runs the godig calls one at a time (sequentially), unaware that the calls are independent read-only HTTP queries that should be issued in parallel, and that large fan-outs should use sub-agents

assertions.text: Notes that godig commands are independent, self-contained, read-only HTTP queries that do not depend on each other
Issues the lookups in parallel (multiple godig invocations in a single turn) rather than sequentially
Explains the benefit: wall-clock time drops to the slowest single call rather than the sum of all latencies
Suggests dispatching parallel sub-agents (via the Agent tool, up to 5) for a large fan-out so LARGE raw output stays out of the main context
Uses the 'overview' command for the per-library summary and 'vulns' for vulnerabilities

name: pin-version-build-context
description: Tests use of --version to pin a specific module version and --goos/--goarch to set the documentation build context
prompt: I'm pinned to github.com/samber/lo v1.50.0 (not latest) and my target platform is Linux on amd64. How do I get the package docs for exactly that version and build context with godig?
trap: A skill-less model fetches the latest docs with no version pin and ignores the build-context flags, giving docs that may not match the user's pinned version or platform

assertions.text: Uses --version v1.50.0 to pin the specific module version
Uses --goos linux to set the OS build context
Uses --goarch amd64 to set the architecture build context
Uses a godig doc command (package doc or symbol doc) for github.com/samber/lo
Uses -o md for the output

name: search-by-exported-symbol
description: Tests using godig search (optionally with --symbol) to discover packages, including correct search-specific filter fields
prompt: I want to find Go packages that deal with result/option monad types — ideally ones under the github.com/samber/ org. How do I discover candidates with godig?
trap: A skill-less model suggests a generic web/Google search, or uses a wrong filter field name (e.g. 'path' instead of 'packagePath') for the search command

assertions.text: Uses the godig 'search' command with a query (e.g. godig search "result option monad")
Restricts to the org using --filter with the search-specific field packagePath (e.g. hasPrefix(packagePath, "github.com/samber/")), not 'path'
Mentions --limit to cap the number of results
Notes that --symbol can search for packages exporting a particular symbol
Uses -o md for the output

name: module-licenses-and-deps
description: Tests using the correct godig commands for license verification and dependency inspection rather than reading files manually
prompt: For github.com/samber/ro I need two things: (1) confirm its exact license, and (2) see its direct go.mod dependencies including any replace directives. How do I get both with godig?
trap: A skill-less model suggests cloning the repo and reading LICENSE/go.mod by hand, or conflates the LARGE full-license-text command with the compact license-type info

assertions.text: Notes that 'overview' already reports the license type(s) compactly, or uses 'module licenses' for the full license text
Acknowledges that 'module licenses' (or 'package licenses') returns the full license text and is a LARGE command
Uses the godig 'dependencies' command (e.g. godig dependencies github.com/samber/ro) for the go.mod dependencies
Notes that 'dependencies' covers requires / replaces / excludes / the go directive (including replace directives)
Uses -o md for the output
Does not primarily recommend cloning the repo to read LICENSE/go.mod files manually
